battle.name: 墨西哥獨立戰爭
battle.theater: 瓜納華托高原與墨西哥城
battle.brief: 一八一〇年九月十六日，瓜納華托的多洛雷斯教堂鐘響，牧師伊達爾戈點燃新西班牙的起義；十一年後伊圖爾維德率三保證軍進城，宣告獨立。皇家軍的野砲在山脊上以霰彈射程打散密集的義軍縱隊，義軍手上卻多是獵槍、柴刀與火繩槍——那件要點火、要瞄、要排隊的舊火器，正是散兵最難練成的形制。

kit.name: 火繩槍
kit.history: 火繩槍要點火、要瞄、要排隊。方陣把這些弱點變成了整齊的彈幕。

countries: 墨西哥獨立戰爭寫在紙上是新西班牙對西班牙本土的戰爭，實際上是同一片殖民地裡由兩套國家機器互相開火。西班牙一方在拿破崙入侵之後國體震盪，一八〇八至一八一三年間由塞維拉最高執委會、卡迪茲攝政廷與卡迪茲代表大會輪流主持國家，一八一四年費爾南多七世復辟後重拾專制，遠征美洲的船隊自加的斯出發。新西班牙總督區由總督兼都督統轄，一八一三至一八二三年在任的是比爾多·哈維斯·德·文特薩；軍令自馬德里經阿卡普爾科與韋拉克魯斯兩條海路傳入，基層則靠各都督區的省督、軍務會議與市鎮民兵維持秩序。野戰主力是西班牙殖民常備軍與各都督區民兵：步兵線列以早已淘汰火繩、裝用燧發滑膛槍（pedrería）的方陣為主，配刺刀與長矛；炮兵分輕型野砲與中型攻城砲；騎兵為輕騎兵與龍騎，用長矛、軍刀與馬槍。起義一方則分三段建制：第一段是一八一〇年九月起於城市與礦區的群眾性起義，領袖是教區神甫，沒有編制，靠教會鐘聲、佈告與礦工糾合號召人馬；第二段是南北兩支義軍的正規化，中西部歸莫雷洛斯，南方歸一批在戰場上自行升遷的旅長，軍中設委員會議定軍令；第三段是一八二一年伊圖爾維德與維森特·格雷羅合流後成立的三保證軍，以營連編制的線列步兵為骨架，編有炮兵、騎兵與隨軍工匠，並配軍需官與輜重隊，接納各地起義部隊為附屬兵團。西班牙方面的關鍵變數在歐洲：半島上拿破崙戰爭的勝負，直接決定母國還能向新西班牙派出多少兵、留多少船。
countriesEn: On paper the Mexican War of Independence was a war between New Spain and metropolitan Spain; on the ground it was two state apparatuses firing at each other inside a single colony. On the Spanish side, the body politic was convulsed after Napoleon's invasion. From 1808 to 1813 the state was run in turn by the Supreme Junta of Seville, the Regency of Cadiz and the Cortes of Cadiz; when Ferdinand VII was restored in 1814 he returned to absolutism, and the fleets sent across the Atlantic departed from Cadiz. The Viceroyalty of New Spain was governed by a viceroy who also held the captain-general's command: from 1813 to 1823 that was the Count of Revillagigedo, Francisco Javier de Venegas. Orders travelled from Madrid by the two sea routes through Acapulco and Veracruz, while day-to-day control rested with the provincial governors, the military councils of each captaincy-general, and the town militias. The field army of the crown consisted of the colonial regular troops and the provincial militias: line infantry formed in squares with flintlock smoothbore muskets (pedreria), the matchlock having long been abandoned, armed with bayonets and pikes; the artillery was split between light field pieces and medium siege guns; the cavalry were light horse and dragoons, with lances, sabres and carbines. The insurgent side passed through three stages. The first was the popular rising that began in the towns and mining districts in September 1810, led by parish priests, without any establishment of units, relying on church bells, proclamations and the muster of mine crews. The second was the regularisation of the two great insurgent armies of the centre-west and of the south, with Morelos in command in the former, a set of colonels who had risen on the battlefield holding the latter, and committees of war issuing orders. The third was the Army of the Three Guarantees formed in 1821 after Iturbide and Vicente Guerrero joined hands: a skeleton of linear infantry organised in battalions and companies, with artillery, cavalry and travelling artificers, a commissariat and a baggage train, absorbing the regional rebel bands as attached brigades. The decisive Spanish variable lay in Europe: the fortunes of the Peninsular War determined how many men and how many ships the mother country could still send to New Spain.
people: 這場戰爭由牧師起、由將軍收。伊達爾戈（一七五三至一八一一年）原是多洛雷斯教區的神甫，一八一〇年九月十六日在瓜納華托的教堂前敲鐘高呼，隨後自任將軍率領城鄉義軍；他沒有受過軍事訓練，卻在幾個月內打下數座礦城，最後在奇瓦瓦被處決，留下的軍隊由莫雷洛斯接手。莫雷洛斯（一七六五至一八一五年）原是米卻肯地方軍的少校，參與過反對維爾多統治的陰謀而遭流放，返回後加入起義，被推為全軍最高將軍，一八一三年寫下《民族情感》，宣示廢除奴隸制與土地歸還原主，一八一五年六月二十二日在奇瓦瓦被槍斃。他的陣亡令第一階段崩潰，戰爭沉寂數年。伊圖爾維德（一七八三至一八二四年）原為墨西哥城區殖民軍少校，得知維爾多死後轉投起義，一八二一年二月提出《伊瓜拉三保證計畫》，主張以天主教、獨立與統一三項保證換取各派合作；格雷羅（一七八二至一八二九年）則是南方最難纏的游擊統帥，兩人於一八二一年二月在阿卡特姆潘相擁結盟，合組三保證軍，最終迫使西班牙總督奧多諾霍簽署《科爾多瓦條約》並退出新西班牙。西班牙方面的關鍵人物是皇家軍統帥卡列哈，以及一八二一年才抵達的總督奧多諾霍。北方線上還有自西班牙渡海而來的自由戰士米納，他一八一七年登陸後節節抵抗，一八一八年在奇瓦瓦被槍斃，他記述美洲戰爭的書信在倫敦出版，成為後世研究民兵戰術的重要文本。婦女同樣在場：萊奧納·比卡里奧供應糧食與信件，約瑟法·奧爾蒂斯·多明格斯在北部策動郡府改弦，瑪麗婭·伊格納西婭·羅德里格斯把城內情報送出城外。在更遠的地方，玻利瓦爾自秘魯致書墨西哥代表，歐洲的觀察家也把新西班牙的戰況與歐洲革命連在一起看。
peopleEn: This war was begun by a priest and finished by a general. Hidalgo (1753-1811), a parish priest of Dolores, rang the bell and raised the cry at Guanajuato on 16 September 1810 and then marched as general with the town and countryside insurgents of the surrounding districts. He had no military training, yet within a few months his columns took several mining towns; he was finally executed at Chihuahua, and the army he had raised passed into the hands of Morelos. Morelos (1765-1815) was a captain in the Michoacan local troops who had been exiled for taking part in a conspiracy against the rule of Virrey, returned, joined the rising and was raised to the rank of generalissimo. In 1813 he drafted the Sentiments of the Nation, proclaiming the abolition of slavery and the restitution of lands to their original owners; on 22 June 1815 he was shot at Chihuahua. His death collapsed the first phase of the war, and several years of quiet followed. Iturbide (1783-1824), a captain in the Mexico City colonial garrison, came over to the insurgents after the news of the fall of Virrey, and in February 1821 published the Plan of the Three Guarantees at Iguala, offering religion, independence and union as the price of reconciliation between factions. Guerrero (1782-1829) was the most tenacious guerrilla commander of the south; the two men embraced at Acatempan in February 1821, formed the Army of the Three Guarantees, and in the end forced the Spanish viceroy O'Donoju to sign the Treaty of Cordoba and withdraw from New Spain. The key men on the Spanish side were the royalist commander Calleja and the viceroy O'Donoju, who only arrived in 1821. On the northern front there was also Francisco Xavier Mina, the Spanish liberal who crossed the sea to join the insurgents, landed in 1817, resisted stubbornly, and was shot at Chihuahua in 1818; his letters describing the war in the Americas were published in London and became an important text for later study of militia tactics. Women were present too: Leona Vicario supplied food and messages, Josefa Ortiz de Dominguez worked to turn the northern cabildos, and Maria Ignacia Rodriguez smuggled intelligence out of Valladolid. Further abroad, Bolivar wrote to Mexican representatives from Peru, and European observers read the fighting in New Spain as part of the same story as the revolutions in Europe.
kits: 卡面這件一五二〇年的火繩槍，落到一八一〇至一八二一年這場戰爭裡，位置既尷尬又關鍵。西班牙本土在十七世紀末已完成由火繩改燧石的換裝，殖民地軍隊的制式步槍早就是燧發滑膛槍，線列步兵的密集射擊完全依賴燧石擊火；火繩槍在一八一〇年早已退出現役，退守省府軍械庫、鄉鎮民兵與莊園警衛的庫房，成為無錢購置新槍者的最後底子。義軍初起時真正持槍者只是少數，多數人只有獵槍（escopeta de caza）、柴刀、削尖的木矛與農具，因此軍械方面的描述常是半數人拿獵槍、半數人拿棍棒。火繩槍在這種環境裡反而有兩項優勢：結構簡單，火藥池、蛇形夾與點火繩都能在鄉間隨手修整，不必依賴精製的擊錘；缺點是射速低、夜間與雨夜不可用、槍身重而長，必須架槍托瞄準，齊射節奏全靠教練維持。起義初期沒有教練，火繩槍常常只是象徵性的有槍——一八一〇年九月瓜納華托阿隆迪加·德·格拉納迪塔斯糧倉之戰正是反面教材：義軍以人潮圍住石造糧倉，攻門不計傷亡，等到守軍把砲架在屋頂、以霰彈和步槍覆蓋街面，人群便成活靶，自己也暴露在毫無遮蔽的正面。皇家軍方面，砲兵使用四磅與六磅的輕型野砲以及短身臼砲，在近距離以霰彈對付密集縱隊；步兵用燧發步槍配刺刀，騎兵用龍騎馬槍與軍刀。後勤上，義軍的槍械與火藥在後期越來越依賴外部輸入：北線經布拉索斯與墨西哥灣的商路購得，內陸義軍則靠走私隊伍翻越山脈輸送，缺彈的問題幾乎貫穿始終。三保證軍成立後才第一次有制度化的軍械供應：按營編制、隨軍軍械官、按月發薪、設修械所，火繩槍這類舊槍在整編中被大量收編，或作為民兵與城防的配件繼續留用。
kitsEn: The matchlock musket on this card, dated 1520, sits in an awkward and yet decisive position in a war fought between 1810 and 1821. Spain completed the changeover from match to flint in the late seventeenth century, and the colonial army's regulation infantry musket was already a flintlock smoothbore; the massed fire of the line rested entirely on the frizzen pan striking sparks. By 1810 the matchlock had long left active service and had retreated to the provincial arsenals, the town militia stores and the guard rooms of the haciendas, where it remained the last gun a man who could not afford a new musket could reach. In the early rising, only a minority of the insurgents actually carried firearms; most had a hunting gun (escopeta de caza), a machete, a sharpened wooden pike or a farm tool, and the arms of the rebel army are usually described as half hunting guns and half clubs. In that setting the matchlock had two real advantages: it was simple, and pan, serpentine and cord could be repaired in the country without a finely made steel; its disadvantages were low rate of fire, uselessness at night or in the rain, and a long heavy barrel that had to be rested on a rest and aimed, so that the rhythm of a volley depended entirely on drill. The early insurgents had no drill, and the matchlock was often merely symbolic: the fighting at the Alhondiga de Granaditas in Guanajuato in September 1810 is the classic cautionary case. The insurgents ringed the stone granary with a human mass, attacked the door without counting casualties, and once the defenders set their guns on the roof and covered the street with grapeshot and musket fire, the crowd became a target and was itself caught in the open with no cover. On the royalist side the artillery used light four- and six-pounder field pieces and short howitzers, firing grapeshot at close range into dense columns; the infantry carried flintlock muskets with bayonets, and the cavalry used dragoon carbines and sabres. In the logistics, the insurgents came to depend more and more on outside supply: arms and powder were bought along the northern routes through the Bravo and the Mexican Gulf, and carried inland by smuggling parties over the mountains, while the shortage of ammunition ran through the whole war. Only with the Army of the Three Guarantees did organised supply of arms appear: units by battalion, travelling armourers, monthly pay and repair shops, with the old matchlocks absorbed into the new order or left in service as the private weapons of militia and town garrisons.
tactics: 起義頭幾個月的打法幾乎是半島式的群眾叛亂：奪鐘、奪倉、奪槍、奪城，武器不齊而人數眾多，靠夜襲與奇襲製造混亂。瓜納華托一役暴露了這種打法的上限——攻方人潮擠在阿隆迪加糧倉前的狹窄街面，沒有展開，沒有掩體，火力一旦覆蓋便無處可退。真正的戰爭在鄉間展開：義軍分成小股隊伍，專走山路，劫襲孤立的小堡與莊園，在王路上設伏，打完即散，使皇家軍賴以取勝的野砲與密集線列難以施展；莫雷洛斯把這套打法提升為機動戰，他率軍帶著輕型野砲在山區不斷轉移，用一兩週的連續行軍避開正面會戰，同時以圍城拖住城市。他自一八一二年末起自南向北推進，一八一三年秋兵臨普埃布拉城下，包圍近一個月仍被援軍解圍，撤退時損失慘重；一八一四年二月楚皮奧之役與十月安戈斯圖拉之役，義軍在山嶺峽谷的攻守之間來回拉鋸，最終一八一四年十月二十二日安戈斯圖拉一敗，義軍主力潰散，莫雷洛斯僅以數十人逃出。皇家軍的反制是掃蕩與集中兩手並用：以數百至數千人的縱隊沿主要道路搜剿，設立聯防據點與軍堡，把鄉民強迫集中到有守備的城鎮，摧毀義軍可資利用的糧食與牲畜，並強迫居民充當嚮導搜索山區。北方戰線以嚴酷鎮壓著稱，義軍在當地屢起屢敗。一八二一年三保證軍的做法完全不同：不再靠烏合之眾，而是以有給糧、有軍籍、有指揮體系的縱隊行軍，沿維拉克魯斯至哈利帕、普埃布拉至墨西哥城約四百公里的王路推進，途中不與敵軍決戰，而以政治宣言、招撫與接管行政為主；最終於九月二十七日入城，九月二十八日簽署《墨西哥帝國獨立宣言》，以談判與儀式完成了群眾起義未能完成的目標。
tacticsEn: For the first months the rising fought in the classic peninsular manner of a popular insurrection: seize the bell, seize the storehouse, seize the muskets, seize the town, with unequal weapons but great numbers, and confusion produced by night attacks and surprises. The fighting at Guanajuato exposed the ceiling of that method: the attackers were packed into the narrow street in front of the Alhondiga granary, undeployed and without cover, and once firepower swept that street there was nowhere to retreat to. The real war was fought in the countryside. The insurgents broke into small bands that kept to the mountain paths, raided isolated forts and haciendas, ambushed along the royal roads and dispersed after contact, so that the field artillery and close-order formations on which the royalists relied could hardly be brought to bear. Morelos turned this into mobile war: he led columns with light field guns that never stopped moving through the highlands, shifted position over one or two weeks of marching to avoid pitched battle, and meanwhile pinned cities down with sieges. From late 1812 he drove north from the south; in the autumn of 1813 he stood before Puebla, besieged it for close to a month, was relieved by a royalist relief force and lost heavily while withdrawing. In the fighting in the ravines and mountains around Chupio in February 1814 and Angostura in October 1814, attack and defence shifted back and forth; the collapse came at Angostura on 22 October 1814, where the insurgent main force was destroyed and Morelos escaped with only a few dozen men. The royalist counter-insurgency used sweeping columns and concentration at once: columns of several hundred to several thousand men searching along the main roads, garrison posts and blockhouses, the forced concentration of the rural population in defended towns, destruction of the food and livestock the insurgents relied on, and the use of local people as guides to search the mountains. The northern front was known for severe repression, and the insurgents there rose and were broken again and again. The Army of the Three Guarantees in 1821 worked on a completely different principle: not a mob but a column with pay, rolls and a chain of command, advancing along the royal road for some four hundred kilometres from Veracruz through Xalapa and Puebla to Mexico City, avoiding pitched battle on the way and relying instead on proclamations, amnesty and the taking over of administration. It entered the capital on 27 September; on 28 September the Act of Independence of the Mexican Empire was signed, and negotiation and ceremony finished what a popular rising could not.
data: 可以核對的數字並不多，以下幾項在各方記載中較為一致。時間上，起義起於一八一〇年九月十六日，首都易手於一八二一年九月二十七日，獨立宣言簽於九月二十八日，全戰爭歷時十一年零十二天，通常分為一八一〇至一八一五與一八一五至一八二一兩個階段。人口方面，一八一〇年新西班牙總人口約六百八十萬，其中原住民佔絕大多數，任何一方能動用的兵力都受這個人口與地理的框限。兵力方面，殖民常備軍與各地民兵合計約一萬人上下，實戰中常集中於數千人的縱隊：一八一二年初卡爾德隆橋一役，皇家軍出動約一千八百人並配數門野砲，義軍則是數萬計的散兵；一八一四年楚皮奧與安戈斯圖拉兩役，雙方投入大致各在數千人之譜。全戰役的戰鬥與圍城以數百計，但單次投入常不超過數千，說明這是一場以小縱隊與游擊為主的戰爭。一八二一年西班牙從本土派出的遠征軍規模約三萬人，真正抵達新西班牙的約萬餘人；三保證軍入城時連同民兵約一萬五千至一萬六千人，並攜有十數門野砲。距離方面，維拉克魯斯至墨西哥城的王路約四百公里，途中要翻越東馬德雷山脈的哈利帕山口；一八一〇年九月伊達爾戈率眾由多洛雷斯走到瓜納華托約五十公里只需數日，而一八二一年三保證軍自哈利帕推進至普埃布拉、再至首都則走了數週。技術面上，阿隆迪加糧倉守軍不過數百人，卻居高臨下，以數門砲的霰彈覆蓋正面；普埃布拉與墨西哥城牆厚、城高、門設鹿角與射孔，起義軍屢攻不下。最後是航運與銀流：馬尼拉至阿卡普爾科的帆船每年一到兩班，單程約兩三個月；新西班牙每年有大批銀幣經海路運往馬尼拉，戰爭期間軍費需求令墨西哥城鑄幣廠超負荷運作，戰後這條銀流改由私人商船分批承運。
dataEn: Few of the numbers can be checked against each other, and the following are the ones on which the accounts broadly agree. In time: the rising began on 16 September 1810, the capital changed hands on 27 September 1821, and the declaration of independence was signed on 28 September; the war therefore lasted eleven years and twelve days and is conventionally divided into a first phase from 1810 to 1815 and a second from 1815 to 1821. In population: New Spain had about 6.8 million inhabitants in 1810, the great majority of them indigenous, and the manpower available to either side was bounded by that population and by the geography. In troops: the colonial regular army together with the provincial militias came to roughly ten thousand men, and in the field they were normally concentrated in columns of several thousand. At the bridge of Calderon in early 1812 the royalists brought out some eighteen hundred men with several field guns against tens of thousands of undisciplined insurgents; at Chupio and at Angostura in 1814 the forces engaged on each side were in the order of several thousand. The war as a whole numbers in the hundreds of battles and sieges, yet few of them involved more than a few thousand men, which shows that it was a war of small columns and of guerrilla action. The expedition sent from Spain in 1821 was on the scale of thirty thousand men, of whom some ten thousand or so actually reached New Spain; the Army of the Three Guarantees counted between fifteen and sixteen thousand men with attached militia when it entered the capital, together with a dozen-odd field guns. In distance: the royal road from Veracruz to Mexico City runs about four hundred kilometres and has to cross the mountains of the Sierra Madre Oriental above Xalapa; in September 1810 Hidalgo's column covered the fifty-odd kilometres from Dolores to Guanajuato in a matter of days, whereas in 1821 the Three Guarantees took some weeks to move from Xalapa to Puebla and on to the capital. In technical terms: the garrison of the Alhondiga granary numbered only a few hundred men, but it held the high ground and covered the front with grapeshot from several guns; Puebla and Mexico City had thick walls, high works and gates furnished with barricades and loopholes, and the insurgents failed to take them. Finally, shipping and silver: the Manila galleons ran from Acapulco once or twice a year and took two or three months each way; large quantities of silver coin left New Spain for Manila by sea, the demands of the war put the Mexico City mint under heavy strain, and after the peace that silver flow was carried in separate instalments by private merchantmen.
cause: 一八一〇年的新西班牙並不是突然決定要造反，它是西班牙本土危機在新大陸上的一連串投影。第一層是王位危機：拿破崙在一八〇八年廢黜波旁王室，西班牙陷入半島戰爭，母國自顧不暇；一八一二年卡迪茲代表大會頒布憲法，宣稱美洲屬地同樣享有主權，一八一四年費爾南多七世復辟後又宣布廢除這部憲法並拒絕承認美洲的自治，等於親手堵死了溫和派的出路。第二層是日常治理的衝突：殖民地每年被徵發送往半島的兵員以數千計，被徵者多為原住民與混血農民，長期遠離家鄉；repartimiento 強制攤派、什一稅、礦業稅與各種附加稅壓在村鎮，而礦產在歐洲戰亂中需求不穩，一八〇八年的地震又重創瓜納華托與塔巴爾卡的礦場，礦工大批失業。教會與地方精英在巴亞多利德（一八〇九年）與托萊多（一八一〇年）的陰謀屢遭破獲，示範了起義可能帶來的後果。第三層是地方社會結構：莊園、什一稅與種族等級令鄉民對殖民政府積怨已久，原住民村社在南部與西部尤其反對土地被圈佔。導火線則是具體的人與地方：一八一〇年九月十六日伊達爾戈在多洛雷斯決定起義，瓜納華托一帶礦工正因礦場蕭條與徵兵而躁動，教堂鐘聲一響，整個墨西哥城區在數週內相繼響應；瓦哈卡、墨西哥城、普埃布拉、聖路易斯波托西、瓜達拉哈拉等地的起義接連爆發，義軍的隊伍在一年內就從數百人擴到數萬人。
causeEn: New Spain in 1810 did not suddenly decide to revolt; it was a series of reflections in New Spain of the crisis in metropolitan Spain. The first layer was the crisis of the throne: Napoleon deposed the Bourbon dynasty in 1808 and Spain was swallowed by the Peninsular War, and the mother country had no strength to defend its colonies. The Cortes of Cadiz promulgated a constitution in 1812 holding that the American territories enjoyed sovereignty in their own right; when Ferdinand VII was restored in 1814 he annulled that constitution and refused the autonomy of the Americas, closing the door on the moderate party with his own hand. The second layer was the friction of everyday government: several thousand men were levied in the colony every year for service in the peninsula, most of them indigenous and mestizo peasants sent far from home; the repartimiento levy, the tithe, the mining tax and a range of surcharges weighed on the villages, while demand for the mines was unstable in the turmoil of Europe and the earthquake of 1808 badly damaged the workings at Guanajuato and Taxco, throwing thousands of miners out of work. Conspiracies among the clergy and the local elite at Valladolid in 1809 and at Toledo in 1810 were repeatedly uncovered, and showed what an insurrection could bring. The third layer was local social structure: the hacienda, the tithe and the system of caste had long made the countryside resentful of colonial government, and the indigenous pueblos of the south and west were especially hostile to the loss of their lands. The trigger was concrete, in particular people and places: on 16 September 1810 Hidalgo resolved to rise at Dolores, the miners around Guanajuato were already restive because the mines were idle and the recruiting was pressing, and when the church bell rang the whole Mexico City region answered within weeks. Revolts broke out in succession at Oaxaca, Mexico City, Puebla, San Luis Potosi, Guadalajara and elsewhere, and the insurgent columns grew from a few hundred men to tens of thousands within a year.
impact: 這場戰爭的結果之一，是約三百年西班牙在新大陸的統治走到盡頭，新西班牙在帝制框架下成為獨立的墨西哥帝國，隨後在一八二二年的一場政變後轉為共和國，一八二四年制憲，正式步入獨立國家的序列。軍事上，它留下兩樣東西：一是伊達爾戈與莫雷洛斯開創的群眾起義傳統，把九月十六日變成國家的年度儀式；二是一八二一年三保證軍的建制經驗——有軍籍、有發薪、有軍需、有縱隊作戰的軍隊，配合政治宣言與談判，最終比任何一次攻城都更有效地終結母國的統治，這套做法後來成為墨西哥國家軍隊的骨架。國際上，新西班牙的脫離重排了美洲的權力平衡：玻利瓦爾在南美洲的事業得到啟發與實際支援，玻利瓦爾本人從南美洲向北方致信並接待墨西哥代表，中美洲與加勒比地區的群眾運動接連興起；而墨西哥的脫離也令美國西南邊界問題變得尖銳，亞當斯與奧尼斯條約確定的西界線、得克薩斯作為流亡者與走私者的天堂，以及一八二八年的美墨邊界條約，構成了此後二十年的邊境糾紛。經濟上，維拉克魯斯港在戰後成為對外貿易的窗口，馬尼拉帆船的壟斷被打破，進口布料、鐵器與火藥湧入，同時本土白銀外流與進口品泛濫並存，一八二〇年代墨西哥的商業化速度加快。損失主要落在莊園、屯倉與村落上，戰爭的實物損失與徵發使新西班牙財政透支，國家在獨立之時已債台高築，這一財政困境正是日後頻繁政變與對外戰爭的底色之一。
impactEn: One of the outcomes of this war was the end of roughly three centuries of Spanish rule on the mainland of the Americas, with New Spain becoming the independent Empire of Mexico inside a monarchical frame, turning into a republic after the coup of 1822, and being given a written constitution in 1824, so entering the ranks of sovereign states. Militarily it left two things behind: the tradition of popular insurrection opened by Hidalgo and Morelos, which turned 16 September into a national annual rite; and the institutional experience of the Army of the Three Guarantees of 1821, an army with rolls, pay, a commissariat and marching columns, which combined with political proclamations and negotiation to end metropolitan rule more effectively than any siege had done, and which later provided the skeleton of the Mexican national army. Internationally, the departure of New Spain rearranged the balance of power in the Americas. Bolivar's undertaking in South America received both encouragement and real support, Bolivar himself wrote northward from South America and received Mexican emissaries, and popular movements followed one another in Central America and the Caribbean. Mexico's separation also sharpened the question of the United States' southwestern border: the western line fixed by the Adams-Onis treaty, Texas as a haven for exiles and smugglers, and the 1828 treaty of limits between Mexico and the United States shaped two decades of frontier dispute. Economically, the port of Veracruz became the window of foreign trade after the war; the monopoly of the Manila galleons was broken, imported cloth, iron and powder flooded in, and at the same time domestic silver drained away alongside the spread of foreign goods, so that the commercialisation of Mexico accelerated through the 1820s. The losses fell mainly on haciendas, storehouses and villages, and the material destruction and requisitions of the war left the finances of New Spain drained; the country began its independence already loaded with debt, and that fiscal distress is one of the underlying colours of the frequent coups and foreign wars that followed.
result: 戰爭以談判收場，而不是以一場決定性會戰收場。西班牙總督奧多諾霍一八二一年八月抵達維拉克魯斯，與伊圖爾維德在拉孔塞爾達會談，二十四日簽署《科爾多瓦條約》，承認新西班牙脫離宗主國；接著三保證軍進入首都，九月二十七日伊圖爾維德的軍隊列隊入城，二十八日市政廳召開制憲會議，同日簽署《墨西哥帝國獨立宣言》，二十九日在大教堂舉行儀式，國旗自此懸於宮牆之巔。伊圖爾維德被各省代表推舉為皇帝，一八二二年加冕，一八二三年退位被推翻，一八二四年遭處決。西班牙在美洲的第一個王國就這樣失去，其餘殖民地在一八二一年之後相繼脫離，西班牙王室從此再無力重返。對墨西哥自身而言，這場戰爭留下三個難題：一是中央權威與各省的關係，聯邦派與中央派從此糾纏百年；二是教會的地位，《伊瓜拉三保證計畫》以天主教作為團結的代價換來和平，卻把教會與國家的糾葛延續至今；三是邊疆與邊民，得克薩斯、加利福尼亞與新墨西哥的歸屬問題在墨西哥無力防守的十年裡被美國利用，一八三六年得克薩斯脫離、一八四六年的美墨戰爭由此而起。對武器史而言，這也是火繩槍的謝幕：從一五二〇年征服者手中的制式火器，到一八一〇年義軍手裡的舊槍，再到一八二一年被整編為民兵配件，一件兵器在美洲活了三百年，見證了從帝國殖民到民族國家的全部過程。
resultEn: The war ended in negotiation rather than in a decisive battle. The Spanish viceroy O'Donoju reached Veracruz in August 1821 and met Iturbide at La Concordia; on the twenty-fourth they signed the Treaty of Cordoba, by which New Spain was recognised as independent of the mother country. The Army of the Three Guarantees then entered the capital: on 27 September 1821 Iturbide's troops marched into the city in column, on the twenty-eighth the cabildo opened as a constituent assembly and the Act of Independence of the Mexican Empire was signed, and on the twenty-ninth the ceremony was held in the cathedral, with the national flag raised on the walls of the palace. Iturbide was acclaimed emperor by the provincial delegates, crowned in 1822, overthrown and deposed in 1823, and executed in 1824. Spain lost its first kingdom in the Americas in this way; the remaining colonies followed in the years after 1821, and the Spanish crown never returned. For Mexico itself the war left three problems. First, the relation between central authority and the provinces, over which federalists and centralists would argue for a century. Second, the standing of the Church: the Plan of the Three Guarantees bought peace with the Catholic guarantee, and the entanglement of Church and state has lasted to this day. Third, the frontier and its inhabitants: the fate of Texas, California and New Mexico was used by the United States during a decade in which Mexico could not defend the border, and Texas's separation in 1836 and the Mexican-American War of 1846 grew out of it. For the history of arms this was also the exit of the matchlock: from the regulation weapon in the hands of the conquistadors of 1520, to the old gun in the hands of the insurgents of 1810, to the piece absorbed into the militia as an accessory in 1821, one firearm lived for three centuries in the Americas and witnessed the whole passage from empire and colony to nation state.
